run.rulesInOwnWords:
1) Start: sap = [3,6,6,2,2,1], every segment QUIET, loss tally 0. Each cycle runs steps 1-5 in order, and each step is finished for all six segments before the next step starts. Every division rounds down.
Step 1 (Uptake): add that cycle's row of the uptake table to each segment. There is no cap in this step.
Step 2 (Xylem push): go through segments 1 to 6 in order. If a segment's sap is above its holding volume (10,8,12,6,9,7), move the excess into the next segment up and set this segment to exactly its holding volume. Excess from segment 6 leaves the stem and goes on the loss tally. Because the segments are handled in order, one push can set off the next one up.
Step 3 (State check), using sap after step 2: a QUIET segment with sap >= its upper mark (7,6,9,5,7,5) becomes SINK-ACTIVE. A SINK-ACTIVE segment with sap <= its lower mark (3,2,4,2,3,2) becomes QUIET. Otherwise the state stays the same. Each segment changes at most once per cycle, and every change is logged.
Step 4 (Phloem/respiration): work out every amount from the sap at the start of the step: QUIET = sap/4, SINK-ACTIVE = sap/2, both rounded down. Then apply them all at once. Each segment loses its amount. A QUIET segment's amount goes to the loss tally. A SINK-ACTIVE segment's amount goes to segment n-1, except segment 1, whose amount goes to the loss tally. There is no cap, so overfill waits for the next cycle's step 2.
Step 5 (Leaf-drop): if total sap > 38 (strictly), halve every segment (rounded down), add the amount removed to the loss tally, and log the cycle. If the total is 38 or less, nothing happens.
